sections.hook: A function is like a machine: you feed it an input, it applies a rule, and produces exactly one output. In IGCSE Add Maths, functions are the foundation for everything that follows.
sections.core_explanation:
A **function** $f: A \to B$ maps each element $x$ in the domain $A$ to exactly one element $f(x)$ in the codomain $B$.

**Domain and Range:** The domain is the set of all possible inputs; the range is the set of all actual outputs.

**Composite Functions:** $(g \circ f)(x) = g(f(x))$. Apply $f$ first, then $g$.

**Inverse Functions:** $f^{-1}$ undoes $f$. $f^{-1}(f(x)) = x$. A function has an inverse only if it is **one-to-one**.

common_mistakes.mistake: Confusing $fg(x)$ with $gf(x)$ — composition is not commutative.
common_mistakes.correction: Always work from right to left: $fg(x)$ means apply $g$ first, then $f$.

common_mistakes.mistake: Assuming every function has an inverse.
common_mistakes.correction: Only one-to-one functions have inverses. Use the horizontal line test.

summary: A function maps each input to exactly one output.
Domain = allowed inputs, Range = actual outputs.
Composite functions: apply inner first, then outer.
Inverse functions undo the original; only one-to-one functions have inverses.
